verdict.t4: GO for GLM Maya-L decode serving: +64/+68% decode (paired rounds), tier wall -40%, cpu pool /2.1, hit 21.8->78.7%, prefill +42/+43% both rounds. THE PRIZE IS THE AGGREGATED VRAM CAPACITY (4 cards x their own expert caches = 9614 slots vs one card's 1934), converted into VRAM hits that skip the pool entirely.
verdict.t2: NO-GO: -4..-5% decode. Two shards double the slots but leave the stripe's misses on 16-thread pools with 2 serialized submissions; hit 40.5% is not enough to pay for it.
verdict.t4e_equal_capacity_fanout: NO-GO (-20..-25%): the pool is bandwidth-bound, not core-count-bound; splitting it buys nothing while the serialization and striped-admission overhead is real.
verdict.contrast_ds41_p6.4: DS4.1 --tier-cards was NO-GO at every N because its ctl already hit 99.23% - capacity was not its limiter. GLM's ctl hits 21.8%: the same mechanism flips sign because the prize (miss headroom) is 3.6x the cache. This is the confirmation the P6.4 doc section 10 predicted: the live axis was the cache-starved engine.
